text: **CertGate prepares the review of a steel mill inspection certificate against a purchase specification, and proposes release, block or review.
A person in Quality decides.** CertGate never releases material on its own.

**All data in this repository is fictitious.** Siderúrgica Valdemora S.A. (the mill), Talleres Ribera Norte S.L. (the buyer), the grade TRN-355 and the purchase specification ESP-014 are invented for the demo.
The limits in ESP-014 belong to that fictitious company and are **not** the limits of any real standard.
Only these synthetic certificates are ever sent to the model endpoint.

Companion documents: [METRICS.md](METRICS.md) (evaluation, generated) · [DEPLOY.md](DEPLOY.md) (Vercel, for the human) · [CLAIMS.md](CLAIMS.md) (every capability sentence and its proof) · [EVIDENCE-INDEX.md](EVIDENCE-INDEX.md) (where the evidence is).

When a batch of steel arrives at a plant, it comes with a mill certificate (an inspection certificate of the EN 10204 3.1 kind): heat or lot, grade, chemical composition and measured mechanical properties.

text: **Primary user:** goods-in or Quality technician at a mid-size plant that buys certified material.
**Who decides:** the Quality manager who signs the release or the block.
For each case (certificate PDF plus its delivery-note line), CertGate:
row: none: lead-in to the list that follows

text: Validates the files (PDF by magic bytes, size limits, not encrypted, has pages) and records their SHA-256.
Reads the certificate through two channels:
row: none: lead-in to the list that follows

text: the **model channel**: the open model Qwen3.8-27B, served by AMD Token Factory, reads the rendered **page images** of every certificate, digital or scanned, and returns the values as one JSON object;
the **text layer** of a digital PDF, extracted without any model.
A scan has no text layer, so its critical fields need human confirmation, and CertGate says so.
Compares the channels.
A disagreement makes the field unknown and the case goes to review.
Checks internal coherence: heat or lot against the delivery note, expected units and scale jumps, and the printed carbon equivalent against one recomputed from the composition.
The formula's source is cited in [docs/sources/cev-formula.md](docs/sources/cev-formula.md).
Applies deterministic, versioned rules against the spec, with exact decimals (never binary floating point).
Proposes `release`, `block` or `review`, records the person's decision (who, when, why) and exports a run receipt without secrets.
Proposal precedence: a heat mismatch means review; otherwise block > review > release.
Release is proposed only when no review or block condition holds.
A scan is never proposed for release until a person has confirmed every critical field.
**Endpoint:** AMD Token Factory, the AMD compute of the event (OpenAI-compatible; host `developer.amd.com.cn`).

**Model:** requested as `Qwen3.8-27B`; every reply reports it as `self-dploy/Qwen3.8-27B`. Its publisher is the Qwen Team, and its licence, as published by the publisher, is apache-2.0 (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, retrieved 2026-10-13; see [docs/sources/model.md](docs/sources/model.md)).
**What the model does:** it reads the page images of a certificate into the CertGate reading contract: value, unit, status, and the location where it says it found the value.
Requests use temperature 0 and a frozen instruction (SHA-256 `32fad2f9…`).
**What the model never does:** it never decides and never explains.
The text-layer comparison, the coherence checks, the rules and the proposal run in the CertGate backend without any model, and a person decides.
The model's reasoning text is never used or stored.
**How it is shown:**

text: **Shared service.** AMD Token Factory is a shared service.
Per key: about 20–30 requests per minute, 8 concurrent requests, and a rolling daily spend cap read from GET /usage (1, in free credits).
During the human's test it answered 429 (concurrency), 504 from the upstream, and connection timeouts.
In the band's two evaluation runs there were 0 retries and 0 failures.
CertGate keeps at most 2 requests in flight, retries only 429 and 5xx (at most 3 attempts, Retry-After honoured), and waits up to 300 s per attempt.
The provider keeps prompts and outputs for about 2 days, so only synthetic data may be sent.
Before any live reading the page shows that notice, and the server requires the visitor to confirm it.
**Slow readings.** One reading takes about 1 to 4 minutes (52–208 s per certificate in the evaluation).
**Deployed site has no live reading (OI-S2-02).**
The worst case of one live reading is 3 × 300 s + 2 × 120 s = 1140 s, above the 300 s Vercel function duration.
With `VERCEL` set, `/api/live/read` answers 503 "live reading unavailable on the deployed site; live demonstration from the container", and the page says so.
Judge mode works on the deployed site; live reading is demonstrated from the container.
**Live-read limit per instance (OI-S2-01).** The limit is counted on the server, per server instance, in memory.
Measured consequence: two instances with a limit of 2 let 4 readings through (test "the live limit is per instance" in `test/web.test.ts`).
With N instances, the real ceiling is N × `LIVE_READS_PER_HOUR` per hour, all drawn on the same endpoint key.
A shared store behind the same interface (`src/web/limiter.ts`) would make it global.
row: none: design note on a possible change, not a capability

text: **Uploads.** Without `LIVE_ACCESS_CODE`, live reading is limited to the 30 dataset certificates, matched by SHA-256; with it, a visitor's synthetic file can also be read.
The access-code path is tested against a local stub with a test-only code, and no real access code is configured on the band's host.
**cg-003, the ambiguous scan.** The model reads the smudged yield strength confidently as **338** MPa; the true value is 358.
It did so in both completed tuning reads, in the recorded story and in the adversary's probe.
The product therefore proposes **block** (rule failure plus no second channel), never release, and the scan still needs a person to confirm every critical field.
The story card shows what the recorded run shows.
The prompt was not tuned to change this.
**Decimal comma, no unit.** The model sometimes returns a printed CEV with a decimal comma and no unit (`0,41`).
It happened once in each real run, on a different case each time (cg-028 in the implementer run, cg-004 in the auditor's).
The text-layer channel check caught it every time, and the case went to review.
**No model-written explanation.** The model is not asked for an explanation, and the product never shows one.
This deviates from step 7 of the product design (03-DISENO); it was chosen to keep decisions entirely in the deterministic rules (I1).
The case file shows the rule reasons.
**Locations are the model's claim.** The page and fragment where the model says it found a value are labelled "as reported by the model" and are not verified.
On digital PDFs the text layer checks the values, not the locations.
**Hostile duplicate field.** A text layer with a spoofed duplicate of a field (cg-022: "ReH (MPa) 400" while the table says 340) makes that field unknown.
A would-be block becomes review, never release.
**Prompt examples.** The reading instruction's examples reuse values of cg-001 ("0.16", "392", "QA-07"). cg-001 is a tuning and story case, outside the 27-case evaluation.
**Text-layer parser.** It covers the two fictitious certificate layouts of the dataset, not arbitrary mill certificates.
**Cosmetic:** `/favicon.ico` answers 404.

Real model, real endpoint: each run read 27 fictitious certificates (cg-004 … cg-030) through AMD Token Factory.
Definitions follow register D3-05 as amended by R3.1 C-08 … C-11 and C-15. cg-001 … cg-003 were used to tune the prompt and are excluded from both runs.
The two runs are independent: different seats, different clean checkouts, different times.
The landing page shows the figures of the implementer run, and names that run.
Candidate commits: each run names the commit it actually ran (below).
The accepted Stage 3 candidate is `5c904693`.
Between these commits the reading path is identical by diff: the reader's request and parsing, the frozen prompt and the rules.
The later commits changed receipt contents (the F1 snapshot and the "as reported by the model" location label), the UI, the upload policy and the tests.
**False conforming** (the grave error): FC-broad = proposal release where the expected proposal is not release, over all cases whose expected proposal is not release.
FC-strict = release where the expected proposal is block, over the expected-block cases (C-08).
Any false conforming in any real run is a REJECT finding with a root-cause line (C-19).
**Rule abstention** = proposal review with status processed; **failure** = status error, by class; reported separately, each over all evaluated cases (C-09).

**Per-field accuracy** compares the model channel with the correct reading of each critical field: correct, unknown, wrong, invented (a value where the field is absent), and **confident-on-illegible** (a confident value where the correct reading is illegible), counted separately (C-10).
**Seconds and cost per certificate** are over processed cases (status not error), with N; a missing reported cost is unknown, never zero (C-11).
Requests use **temperature 0** (C-12).
The runs are reported side by side, with every per-case proposal difference listed below; a difference is never hidden behind one passing run.

Receipts and run artifacts carry the endpoint reply's id, created time, model and usage as returned (C-14); GET /usage is read before and after each run and reconciled with the sum of per-reply costs (C-15).
The tuning cases **cg-001, cg-002 and cg-003** are excluded from the evaluation (D3-03); they are the judge-mode stories.
